transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-09
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood), Diego Morales (Redwood), Ava Nguyen (Redwood), Priya Kapoor (CloudMall), Liam O'Connor (CloudMall), Sofia Chen (CloudMall), Marcus Lee (CloudMall)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Discussed listing on CloudMall marketplace, reference architecture for Private/VPC deployment, KMS and key management flow, security artifacts needed, and next steps for a pilot and co-marketing.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 55 minutes, so we'll try to cover marketplace listing requirements, a reference architecture for the private deployment, and security + next steps. Quick intros?
00:22 Speaker 2 (Priya): Hi, I'm Priya, Head of Partnerships at CloudMall. We're excited to get Redwood live on the marketplace. We've had some partners integrate but this is our first inference provider so, uh, welcome.
00:36 Speaker 3 (Diego): Thanks Priya. Diego here, Solutions Engineer at Redwood. I'll mostly drive the tech bits. Ava is here for any infra questions.
00:45 Speaker 4 (Ava): Hey all.
00:48 Speaker 2 (Priya): Great, Liam, Marcus, Sofia from our side?
00:52 Speaker 5 (Liam): Liam O'Connor, Solutions Architect for partner integrations. We'll own the VPC peering side and infra validation.
00:58 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Marcus Lee, security — I'll be the security reviewer.
01:03 Speaker 7 (Sofia): Sofia Chen, product, and I'll coordinate GTM one-pager and co-branding.
01:10 Speaker 1 (Samira): Awesome. First item: marketplace listing. Priya, can you run through the CloudMall requirements at a high level?
01:20 Speaker 2 (Priya): Sure. We need a listing doc, screenshots, a 1-2 page solution brief, a support contact, pricing SKU and metering plan. Also legal / procurement needs a SOC2 or ISO attestation, and some partners need model of support SLA or a commitment. The listing process itself has a vendor validation stage — we collect security artifacts and a partner contract.
01:39 Speaker 3 (Diego): Great, for pricing we typically offer hosted API pricing and a dedicated SKU for reserved capacity. On the marketplace we can expose both: a hosted monthly plan and a dedicated reserved instance SKU. A question — does CloudMall support marketplace metered billing for per-token usage or only flat monthly SKUs?
01:59 Speaker 5 (Liam): We support both but the finance team prefers single SKU for enterprise on-boarding; metered billing requires additional integration. It's doable though.
02:12 Speaker 1 (Samira): Noted. We'll prepare both options and recommended default. Next, reference architecture — Diego you wanna sketch our proposed flows?
02:22 Speaker 3 (Diego): Yeah. So for CloudMall private / managed offering, recommended is: customer deploys Redwood Private in their VPC (or we deploy in a customer-managed VPC), we support KMS integration (customer KMS or Redwood-managed with HSM), and set up VPC peering or PrivateLink for network connectivity. For the marketplace, we propose a reference arch where CloudMall lists a 'Redwood Private' offering that kicks off an onboarding flow — the end result is the same: network connectivity, keys, and audit log forwarding.
03:01 Speaker 5 (Liam): Quick clarifying question — does Redwood require any egress to public endpoints for model downloads or image pulls? Our infra team needs to know the outbound surface area.
03:12 Speaker 3 (Diego): Good point. If customer uses Redwood Private with an on-prem or air-gapped deployment, we can provide offline bundles for initial model artifacts; for VPC deployments we typically pull models from our artifact registry which resides in a peered account. There's a small bootstrap egress needed for the initial model pulls unless you use the offline option.
03:31 Speaker 6 (Marcus): From security perspective, we need to see encryption-at-rest, key rotation policy, audit logs, and whether PII could appear in logs. Also SOC2.
03:44 Speaker 1 (Samira): Absolutely. We have SOC2 Type II and can share the summary + control matrix. For logs, we can forward structured audit logs to customer's SIEM, and sensitive payloads can be redacted or excluded from logs depending on configuration.
03:58 Speaker 6 (Marcus): How about KMS options — do you support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, or only Redwood-managed?
04:06 Speaker 3 (Diego): We support both. In VPC/private deployments we prefer customer-managed KMS so keys never leave your account. We also support HSM-backed KMS integrations for higher assurance.
04:18 Speaker 2 (Priya): For the marketplace listing, what artifacts do you need from us?
04:25 Speaker 5 (Liam): We need the marketplace product listing template filled, logo, solution brief, support SLA, and security attestation. Priya, I'll email the template after the call.
04:36 Speaker 2 (Priya): Cool.

06:10 Speaker 3 (Diego): I'll talk through the reference architecture details — diagram: CloudMall network <-> VPC peering <-> Redwood Private cluster. The cluster uses GPUs, supports quantized models, and exposes an internal endpoint for inference. We recommend a NAT gateway for model artifact bootstrap unless offline mode is chosen. For KV caching and prefix caching, those are internal to the runtime and do not leak outside the VPC.
06:42 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Is there any third-party telemetry that Redwood collects by default? Some vendors opt-in to usage collection for performance telemetry.
06:52 Speaker 1 (Samira): We collect minimal telemetry to monitor health and performance; customers can opt-out or route telemetry to their own observability stack. We'll share a telemetry map in the security pack.
07:03 Speaker 5 (Liam): For the marketplace billing integration, do you have a recommended mapping between Redwood plans and CloudMall SKUs?
07:12 Speaker 3 (Diego): Suggested mapping: Basic hosted plan (pay-as-you-go) for SMB customers, Dedicated reserved SKU for enterprise with commit, and an On-Prem / Private SKU that represents an annual license + support. We'll propose default price ranges in the draft listing.
07:29 Speaker 4 (Ava): One operational note — for canary rollouts across multiple customers, we have a routing policy that can failover to a hosted endpoint in a different region if private capacity is constrained. That's important to mention in the listing as an availability feature.
07:48 Speaker 2 (Priya): Good to know. Also procurement will ask about liability and support window, so any standard SLA we can attach?
07:57 Speaker 1 (Samira): We have template SLAs. For Dedicated / Private, we can offer an enterprise SLA as an add-on. We'll include that in the marketplace listing appendix.

15:20 Speaker 5 (Liam): Let's deep dive on KMS handshake — do you support a customer KMS that signs a bootstrap token, or do we exchange certificates?
15:31 Speaker 3 (Diego): We support standard KMS APIs. The flow we usually suggest: customer creates a KMS key, grants Redwood the necessary crypto operations via IAM role or cross-account grant for provisioning, then we never export plaintext keys. For HSM-backed keys, the customer retains control and we call the key for decryption operations in-place. The exact handshake depends on cloud provider.
15:55 Speaker 6 (Marcus): We'll want an architecture doc with the exact IAM permissions and roles to review with our security team.
16:03 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll attach that. Diego, can you own IAM doc?
16:08 Speaker 3 (Diego): Yep, I'll draft the IAM permissions, the KMS policy snippets, and an example CloudFormation/Terraform snippet.

23:40 Speaker 2 (Priya): On the GTM side, Sofia will own a joint one-pager. Any co-marketing assets we should plan?
23:48 Speaker 7 (Sofia): We'll do a co-branded solution brief, a short demo video, and a marketplace banner. Need logo assets and a short product description from Redwood.
24:05 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll provide logos and a 250-word description plus 3 screenshots of the console and a sample API call.
24:15 Speaker 7 (Sofia): Also, is there a 3rd party certification or badge CloudMall can grant? We have a "verified integration" badge but it requires a technical review.
24:27 Speaker 2 (Priya): Yeah we have a verified badge; the requirements are passing an infra checklist and an attestation to support. After that we can promote in the marketplace.

33:10 Speaker 5 (Liam): A couple edge cases — if a customer wants an air-gapped on-prem bundle, what's the process and timeline?
33:21 Speaker 3 (Diego): For air-gapped, we provide an offline package that includes model binaries and container images. It requires more legal review for licensing and around updates; typical turnaround is 4-6 weeks for a customer-ready on-prem package. We'll note that in the reference architecture doc.
33:38 Speaker 6 (Marcus): For audit logs, do you support pushing to customer S3 buckets or to SIEM via syslog?
33:46 Speaker 3 (Diego): Both. We can forward JSON audit logs to an S3 bucket or stream to customer SIEM via our log forwarder. We also support Kafka/HTTP sinks.

41:12 Speaker 1 (Samira): OK let's do a quick recap and assign action items. I'll start — Redwood will share marketplace checklist, reference architecture draft, and a telemetry map.
41:25 Speaker 3 (Diego): I'll take the reference arch and IAM/KMS snippets.
41:30 Speaker 5 (Liam): CloudMall will send network diagrams and marketplace templates. Marcus will send SOC2 artifacts via secure link.
41:38 Speaker 6 (Marcus): I'll circulate the SOC2 summary and encryption control list.
41:43 Speaker 7 (Sofia): I'll draft the one-pager and kick off co-branding with marketing.
41:48 Speaker 2 (Priya): I'll coordinate procurement and legal handoff.

49:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Any blockers?
49:05 Speaker 5 (Liam): None immediate. We need to validate the metered billing path with finance — I'll follow up.
49:12 Speaker 1 (Samira): Great. Proposed next meeting: technical workshop with CloudMall infra team week of May 19. Does that work?
49:21 Speaker 2 (Priya): Works for us.
49:24 Speaker 7 (Sofia): Works.
49:26 Speaker 1 (Samira): Perfect. Thanks everyone. We will send the checklist and draft reference architecture by next Friday.
49:40 Speaker 3 (Diego): Thanks all.
49:44 Speaker 5 (Liam): Thanks.
49:46 Speaker 6 (Marcus): Bye.
